program_overview.title: C++ for Teens
program_overview.tagline: The language that hides nothing: pointers, memory and speed understood for real, then turned into data structures, games and contest-ready code.
program_overview.description:
C++ is the language serious computer science still speaks: competitive programming runs on it, game engines are built in it, and the concepts it refuses to hide, memory, pointers, performance, are exactly what make every later language feel easy. This live online course takes students aged 13 to 18 through it honestly: fundamentals learned patiently, then the famous hard parts, pointers, references and dynamic memory, taught with pictures and patience until they click, object-oriented C++, the STL used the way contests and codebases use it, data structures built by hand, a 2D games month with SFML, and a genuine introduction to competitive programming.

C++ rewards patience more than any beginner language, and the pace respects that: ten months at two live classes a week plus three to four hours of practice, with two more months in hand. What the course refuses to do is tour everything: OpenGL, embedded boards and compiler internals are named honestly as later specializations, not squeezed in as fake weeks.

Homework after every class, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free retest. Real memory, real speed, depth over dopamine.

faqs.question: What will my teen build in this C++ course?
faqs.answer: More than 25 real builds across ten months: console programs and logic games in the fundamentals, pointer-visualized memory exercises, class hierarchies and file-backed applications, hand-built data structures, timed contest sets, a real 2D game in SFML, and a memory-clean capstone presented at demo day.

faqs.question: Is C++ too hard as a first language for a teenager?
faqs.answer: It is harder than Python, and that is precisely its value when taught patiently: C++ hides nothing, so a teen who learns it understands memory, types and performance for life, and every later language feels easy. This course paces the famous hard parts, pointers get pictures and patience, not one rushed lecture, and the 2-month margin exists exactly for them.

faqs.question: How long does it take, and how is my teen assessed?
faqs.answer: Ten months at 2 live classes a week plus 3 to 4 hours of practice, with two more months in hand. Homework follows every class, monthly assignments mix new questions with earlier topics, each phase ends with an exam, and a final exam, practical plus written, decides the certificate with a free retest after revision.

faqs.question: Does this course prepare for competitive programming?
faqs.answer: It builds the exact base: STL fluency, hand-built structures, algorithmic thinking and a genuine contest-foundations month with timed sets. Serious contest training, dynamic programming, advanced graphs, rating grinds, lives in our dedicated DSA course, which this course names honestly as the next road.

faqs.question: C++ or Python first?
faqs.answer: Both are excellent and we teach both. Python first suits teens pulled toward AI and quick wins; C++ first suits teens bound for competitive programming, engineering entrances or school boards that reward its depth, and produces unmatched fundamentals. Nothing learned in either has to be unlearned.
